rationale: The Latin anchor *intendere* (to direct, stretch toward, apply the mind) and the contextual gloss ("animum intendit" — he directed/stretched his mind to what he heard) point to a sense of extending or directing attention outward. The OE *a-þenian* most closely corresponds to "extend or stretch out to a greater or full length" (unfold.v.03), which captures the sense of deliberately directing/extending (the mind or body) rather than passive elongation or mere bodily relaxation. This synset best matches the literal-to-figurative stretch of *intendere* in the Latin source.
